subject: Post-call: private VPC routing, firewall & IP allowlist clarifications
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinson <alex.martinson@netscale.io>, ops@netscale.io
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: private VPC routing, firewall & IP allowlist clarifications

Alex — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the open items so we can align engineering and network ops before the technical deep-dive next week.

High-level outcome:
- NetScale is leaning toward a Private VPC deployment (PrivateLink preferred) to keep traffic off the public internet.
- Primary concerns are egress IPs for third-party APIs, whether PrivateLink or VPC peering fits their multi-account environment, and TLS inspection on the appliance side.

Open questions / action items for NetScale (see inline):
1) PrivateLink vs Peering: Do you require cross-account PrivateLink (we provide interface endpoints) or would you prefer VPC peering and route tables? If cross-account PrivateLink, we need the account ID(s) and whether you want interface endpoints in multiple AZs.
2) Egress model: Will you accept Redwood-managed static egress IPs (we offer a NAT egress block for PrivateLink), or do you need egress to come from your network (SNAT by your NAT gateway)?
3) IP allowlist scope: Please share the minimal CIDR ranges that your security team will allow (we can provide recommended /24 blocks but need confirmation).
4) TLS inspection & proxy: Are you performing TLS inspection on the edge? If so, do you require Redwood to terminate TLS in your VPC or should traffic be passed through an inspection appliance?
5) Network diagram: can you upload a one-page network diagram (VPCs, transit, on-prem links) so we can validate route table and gateway requirements.

Attachments referenced in this thread: netscale-network-draft.pdf (please upload your diagram)

Next steps suggested:
- Alex: share the 1-page diagram and confirm answers to Q1–Q4 by Tue 4/13.
- Redwood (Ben/Karthik): after we get the diagram, schedule a 45-min technical review to map routes and firewall rules.

I attached a short checklist we use for PrivateLink engages (redwood-deploy-checklist.md) and an export of our current PrivateLink egress ranges (redwood-privatelink-ip-ranges.csv) for planning — if NetScale security needs a specific format (CSV vs JSON), let me know.

Thanks — Sofia

--
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Alex Martinson <alex.martinson@netscale.io>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: NetScale Ops <ops@netscale.io>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: private VPC routing, firewall & IP allowlist clarifications

Sofia — thanks for the recap, that matches our notes. Answers below and I attached an initial network sketch.

1) PrivateLink vs Peering: We prefer PrivateLink (cross-account). NetScale runs core infra in a security account (111222333444). We want interface endpoints in two AZs for redundancy.
2) Egress model: We'd like Redwood to advertise static egress IPs (your NAT block). We delegate outbound traffic filtering to our security appliances but need a consistent external source IP for vendor allowlists.
3) IP allowlist scope: We'll accept up to a /24 per region. For now please propose candidate /24s and we'll run them through change control.
4) TLS inspection & proxy: We do TLS inspection in-line with our proxy appliance. We need traffic to exit the PrivateLink endpoint un-terminated (no TLS offload). That means Redwood should not terminate TLS inside our VPC.

Attachment: netscale-network-draft.pdf (network sketch, transit gateway, appliance position).

We'll aim to have any constraints from our firewall team by EOD Wed 4/14.

—Alex
Alex Martinson
Head of Platform Ops | NetScale
alex.martinson@netscale.io | +1 (650) 555-0199

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinson <alex.martinson@netscale.io>, ops@netscale.io
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: private VPC routing, firewall & IP allowlist clarifications

Alex — perfect, this is helpful. Notes and immediate asks for engineering: 

- Cross-account PrivateLink: account ID noted (111222333444). We'll plan for Interface endpoints in two AZs. Karthik, Ben — can you confirm our recommended interface endpoint security group rules and whether we require a cross-account IAM role for endpoint acceptance?
- Egress IPs: we'll propose two candidate /24s for your change control. I'll attach the CSV of our current egress block options (redwood-privatelink-ip-ranges.csv).
- TLS: noted that traffic must remain TLS-wrapped and not terminated in the VPC. We'll confirm our client TLS passthrough behavior for PrivateLink connectors.

Proposed immediate timeline:
- Thu 4/15: Redwood to send candidate /24 egress ranges and a short checklist of security group / route table changes.
- Mon 4/19: 45-min technical deep-dive with NetScale ops + Redwood infra engineers to validate diagram and finalize runbook.

Attachments: redwood-privatelink-ip-ranges.csv, redwood-deploy-checklist.md

If anything changes on your side re: proxy/TLS inspection, flag it before Thu so we can adjust runbook.

Thanks — Sofia

--
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.com

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: quick tech notes before Mon deep-dive (PrivateLink specifics)

Team — quick internal notes so we come prepared for Mon 4/19: 

1) Interface endpoints: plan to request acceptance from their security account (111222333444). Karthik — can you draft the cross-account endpoint policy template and SG recommendations (allow from NetScale subnets only, deny 0.0.0.0/0)?
2) Egress /24 candidates: Ben — please pick two candidate /24s from our reserved pool and confirm they do not overlap with existing customers in us-west-2. I'll attach the CSV we sent.
3) TLS passthrough: Confirm our connector behaves as passthrough (no L4 termination) for PrivateLink. If there are any limitations (e.g., ALPN/HTTP/2), call them out.

Meeting prep: grab their diagram from the Drive link and mark obvious route table changes (local route vs TGW).

Thanks — Sofia

--
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Engineer
